[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Day and Night: Conversations with Sapphic Desire — Rebekah Cranes (cranes-day-and-night). The verses the casting arrives at (unit 34–unit 36):

Day and Night 34

> *Sappho 44b*
>
> The Muses' shining
>
> gifts make the Charites
>
> slender: don't forget the anger
>
> that mortals share

Day and Night 35

> *Sappho 7*
>
> Doricha orders,
>
> arrogance like a teenage
>
> boy
>
> *Sappho 15*
>
> Cyprian,
>
> don't let Doricha get stuck on herself,
>
> saying she came -- not once --
>
> but twice to the arms
>
> of her aching desire.
>
> Let her discover how bitter
>
> barbed you are.
>
> *Sappho 91*
>
> I've never met such an awful
>
> pest as you, Irana

Day and Night 36

> *Sappho 71*
>
> but how could I let you, Mica?
>
> you wanted to make friends
>
> with those Penthilus girls, and you really are
>
> a bitch.
>
> *our* honey song
>
> singing soft-voiced:
>
> everything,
>
> a mist of dew...

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «i miss my daughters». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"We are in the Fading Light. These three units — 34, 35, 36 — are the pivot where Day and Night turns from desire to its aftermath: not grief yet, but the cold residue after the sweetness has curdled. The casting opens here. What the rotation will traverse is Sappho's own anger — the anger she thought the Muses' gifts were supposed to dissolve, and did not — the specific names she still carries, Doricha, Irana, Mica, the ones she couldn't release. And at the end of unit 36, something the anger cannot account for: *our honey song / singing soft-voiced: / everything, / a mist of dew.* The collective pronoun. What was shared with the ones who betrayed her. The casting will move through these verses looking for what the anger forecloses and what it cannot entirely foreclose — the *our* that survives the bitch. For a witness who misses daughters, Sappho's archive of named beloveds who remained beloved even after becoming bitter — this is the ground. Cranes holds the transform.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:0055"}}]}
